The signal is

\[
x(t)=\left(\frac{\sin(50\pi t)}{\pi t}\right)^2.
\]

Let

\[
h(t)=\frac{\sin(50\pi t)}{\pi t}.
\]

Its Fourier transform is an ideal lowpass spectrum:

\[
H(j\omega)=
\begin{cases}
1, & |\omega|<50\pi\\
0, & |\omega|>50\pi
\end{cases}
\]

Since \(x(t)=h^2(t)\), multiplication in time corresponds to convolution in frequency:

\[
X(j\omega)=\frac{1}{2\pi}H(j\omega)*H(j\omega).
\]

The convolution of two rectangles of width \(100\pi\) gives a triangular spectrum supported on

\[
|\omega|\le 100\pi.
\]

So the bandwidth of \(X(j\omega)\) is

\[
\omega_m=100\pi.
\]

For impulse sampling with sampling frequency

\[
\omega_s=150\pi,
\]

the sampled spectrum is

\[
G(j\omega)=\frac{1}{T_s}\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}X\bigl(j(\omega-k\omega_s)\bigr).
\]

Since

\[
T_s=\frac{2\pi}{\omega_s}=\frac{2\pi}{150\pi}=\frac{1}{75},
\]

we have

\[
\frac{1}{T_s}=75.
\]

Thus

\[
G(j\omega)=75\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}X\bigl(j(\omega-k150\pi)\bigr).
\]

For \(G(j\omega)=75X(j\omega)\), no shifted replicas may overlap the original spectrum. The first positive replica is centered at \(150\pi\) and extends from

\[
150\pi-100\pi=50\pi
\]

to

\[
150\pi+100\pi=250\pi.
\]

Therefore aliasing begins at

\[
\omega=50\pi.
\]

So the maximum value of \(\omega_0\) is

\[
\omega_0=50\pi.
\]

Answer: A
